subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a native user-controlled backup exclude surface now, and if so should it include implicit `.backupignore` loading and smart defaults or only explicit CLI-supplied patterns?
rationale: This PR changes a restore-critical backup contract, introduces new public flags and dependency surface, and overlaps current main's newer backup reliability hardening; automation should not choose the permanent backup policy.

options.title: Require a narrowed native contract
options.body: Keep the native feature direction but require explicit persistent-file opt-in, per-asset filtering, current-main rebase, and real backup proof before merge.

options.title: Accept the broader contract
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept smart defaults and `.backupignore` auto-loading, but should document that upgrade/security behavior and own the restore-safety risk.

options.title: Defer to the canonical issue
options.body: Pause or close this implementation and continue product discussion in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/40786 until a smaller contract is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Require a narrowed native contract
recommendation.body: Keep the native feature direction but require explicit persistent-file opt-in, per-asset filtering, current-main rebase, and real backup proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their backup archive extraction history is the strongest owner signal for the core backup runtime boundary touched here.
